transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-20
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Alexis Reed (Elmwood CISO), Tom Alvarez (Elmwood Head of IT), Priya Menon (Elmwood Security Engineer)

Summary:
Quick SOC 2 / ISO 27001 posture review. Elmwood wants to validate Redwood's controls mapping, get redacted reports, confirm trust center access, and clarify KMS / BYOK, RBAC/SSO integration, audit log retention and data residency for PHI workloads. Next steps and controls spreadsheet requested.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, we'll kick off, I'm Jordan Park, AE on the Redwood side, with Maya our SE, and we'll go through our SOC 2 and ISO posture, answer questions.
[00:22] Alexis: Thanks Jordan. I'm Alexis, CISO at Elmwood. We have Tom and Priya here. High-level, we need to know: do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, can we get redacted reports, and how do you map your controls to our compliance reqs? Also KMS/keys, data residency for PHI.
[00:40] Maya: Yep, thanks Alexis. Short answer: we have both SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications. We host the artifacts via our Trust Center; I can share links and a redacted SOC2 PDF. We'll also provide a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps Redwood controls to common frameworks.
[00:55] Tom: What's the Trust Center URL? I couldn't find it earlier.
[01:02] Maya: It's here: https://trust.redwood.com. I'll include the link in the follow-up email. There's a gated access tab for customers where you can request the redacted report and certificates.
[01:15] Priya: Great. On KMS: do you support BYOK or customer-managed keys / HSM? We need to know for encryption at rest for PHI.
[01:27] Maya: We do support BYOK in our Private deployment and Dedicated in certain plans; hosted customers can use Redwood-managed keys with options to integrate with customer KMS via an envelope encryption model. For Private, you can bring keys and integrate with an HSM or cloud KMS. We have documented patterns for AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault.
[01:50] Alexis: Can you confirm whether Redwood-stored logs or audit trails can be exported to our SIEM? Our audit team requires custody of logs for 7 years — is that supported?
[02:05] Jordan: We expose detailed audit logs and can support log forwarding — S3 export, syslog, or direct integration with common SIEMs. Retention is configurable in Dedicated/Private; hosted has standard retention (90 days) but we do have long-term retention add-ons and can sign customers up for extended retention via contract.
[02:25] Priya: 90 days isn't going to cut it for us, we need 7 years. Would that require a Private deployment?
[02:32] Maya: In most cases yes — long-term retention and full custody is usually handled in Private or through our enterprise add-on where we push logs to a customer-owned S3 bucket for retention. We'll map options in the controls spreadsheet.
[02:45] Alexis: Okay. Can you walk us through the controls mapping — like how Redwood maps to SOC 2 CC1-CC7 and ISO 27001 Annex A controls?
[03:00] Maya: Sure. High level: we map our policies and technical controls to SOC 2 Trust Service Criteria — security, availability, confidentiality, processing integrity — and to ISO 27001 Annex A domains. Example: our access control policy + RBAC in the console maps to A.9 and several SOC 2 access control criteria. We'll share the detailed spreadsheet with row-level mappings and evidence links.
[03:25] Tom: Evidence links meaning artifacts in the Trust Center?
[03:29] Maya: Exactly, e.g., policy docs, configuration screenshots, our SOC 2 auditor statements, and where applicable, config exports. Some evidence is redacted for vendor confidentiality but we'll point you to control owners and artifact names.
[03:45] Alexis: On SSO: do you support SAML/SSO and SCIM for provisioning? We need RBAC integration with Okta.
[03:54] Maya: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported. You can connect Okta and provision roles. Our RBAC is role-based and hierarchical — you can map Okta groups to Redwood roles. For sensitive roles, you can enforce step-up authentication or approval workflows.
[04:15] Priya: Any support for conditional access or MFA enforcement from your side?
[04:20] Maya: We enforce session timeouts and support MFA enforcement through SSO providers — so Okta handles MFA policies. We can also enforce stricter session policies on Dedicated/Private.
[04:34] Alexis: Auditability: what fields do you capture in the audit logs? We need user identity, IP, action, resource, timestamps, request payload hashes, and whether content included PHI was accessed.
[04:47] Maya: Our audit logs include user email/ID, timestamp, IP, action type, resource identifier, request id, model used, and success/failure codes. For content-level indicators like PHI tags, Redwood can optionally run detection and flag requests, but by default we don't parse customer payloads for PHI unless enabled — we'll document the options.
[05:10] Tom: About encryption in transit and at rest — what's the algorithm, TLS version, and key rotation cadence?
[05:17] Maya: TLS 1.2+ is required; we recommend 1.3. At rest we use AES-256 with envelope encryption. Key rotation: default CMKs are rotated annually; with BYOK you control rotation cadence via your KMS.
[05:35] Alexis: For the hosted API, is any customer data used for model training or analytics?
[05:42] Jordan: No. For our enterprise and customer-facing policies, we do not use customer-provided content to train models. We have a strict data usage policy and it is reflected in the SOC2 confidentiality criteria and contract terms; we'll include the link to the policy in the Trust Center.
[06:00] Priya: If we require a BAA for HIPAA PHI, do you sign BAAs?
[06:05] Jordan: We do sign BAAs for customers processing PHI — typically customers on Dedicated or Private. We'll route that to legal and include it in the contract discussion.
[06:15] Alexis: Good. On network isolation — in Private or Dedicated, can we restrict egress so logs and keys never leave our VPC?
[06:25] Maya: Yes, Private deployments are fully customer-managed network-wise; Dedicated offers VPC peering and strict routing policies. You can configure egress rules, and for BYOK the keys never leave your KMS.
[06:40] Tom: Do you have penetration test reports / vulnerability scanning evidence in the Trust Center?
[06:47] Maya: We publish summary pentest results and a schedule; full reports are available under NDA in the Trust Center. We also run regular SCA (software composition analysis), vulnerability scanning, and publish the remediation cadence.
[07:05] Alexis: For ISO 27001, who is the certifying body and what's the scope?
[07:11] Maya: Our ISO 27001 certification was issued by DQS and the scope covers our inference platform and control plane services for hosted and dedicated offerings — we'll provide the certificate and declared scope file.
[07:25] Priya: Controls mapping aside, what's the practical difference between Hosted + add-ons vs Dedicated for compliance? Like which controls are possible only on Dedicated?
[07:37] Maya: Hosted can meet many controls through contractual and operational measures — e.g., SOC2, ISO, encryption at rest. However, controls that require customer custody — e.g., long log retention in customer-owned storage, customer-managed KMS without Redwood intermediate keys, strict VPC-only access — often require Dedicated or Private. We'll mark those controls in the spreadsheet as "requires Dedicated/Private".
[07:58] Tom: We heard about continuous caching and KV cash earlier in a demo — any concerns with cached data holding PHI?
[08:06] Maya: Good callout — Redwood has automatic KV cache and prefix caching to improve latency. For PHI workloads, we'd disable persistent caching or ensure it's encrypted and keys are under customer control in Dedicated/Private. We'll document cache behavior and recommendations. Sorry for the earlier transcript typo — sometimes demos say KV cash, ha.
[08:30] Alexis: How do you handle third-party subprocessors and data residency? We need to ensure no data is routed to countries we restrict.
[08:40] Maya: Subprocessors are listed in the Trust Center with regions where they operate. We support region restrictions and can pin workloads to specific cloud regions. For stringent residency, Private on-prem or regional Dedicated is recommended.
[08:55] Priya: About audit log integrity: do you provide tamper-evident logs or signed log chains?
[09:03] Maya: We provide signed log exports and can integrate with append-only storage like S3 with Object Lock for WORM compliance. For higher assurance, customers can use our log-forwarding to their own SIEM or S3 bucket that they control.
[09:20] Tom: In terms of identity federation, does Redwood accept OIDC as well as SAML?
[09:25] Maya: Yes, SAML and OIDC are both supported. SCIM for provisioning, and we map attributes to roles.
[09:33] Alexis: A couple of specific questions from our audit team: 1) Can you provide a controls matrix for SOC 2 CC and ISO Annex A? 2) Evidence for retention and deletion policies? 3) KMS architecture diagram for BYOK?
[09:45] Maya: Yes to all three. We'll provide the controls matrix with evidence pointers; retention and deletion policies are in the DLP and Data Retention docs in Trust Center; and we have a BYOK architecture diagram that shows envelope encryption and HSM integration.
[10:02] Jordan: I'll also flag that for customers requiring PHI & HIPAA we typically recommend Dedicated or Private and we can walk legal teams through BAAs.
[10:10] Priya: For log fields again -- will the logs surface request/response content? We need content redaction options.
[10:18] Maya: By default logs do not contain full request/response bodies in hosted — only metadata and references. If you need full payload retention in Private/Dedicated, that can be enabled, but we provide redaction and tokenization options.
[10:33] Alexis: Any SLAs around incident response and notification windows?
[10:37] Maya: We have incident response commitments in our security policy; standard disclosure windows are 72 hours for confirmed breaches, and we have a 24/7 on-call security team for critical incidents for enterprise customers. We'll include the IR policy excerpt.
[10:55] Tom: Are there contract clauses for right to audit?
[10:59] Jordan: Yes, enterprise contracts include right-to-audit clauses with defined scopes and frequency; audits are scheduled and often executed with auditor coordination.
[11:10] Priya: How granular is RBAC — can we create custom roles with least privilege?
[11:17] Maya: Yes, custom roles are supported and you can scope role permissions to specific models, routes, or projects. You can also set approval gates for sensitive operations.
[11:30] Alexis: Can we get a sample controls mapping row for e.g., encryption at rest?
[11:35] Maya: Sure. Example row: Control: Encryption at rest (SOC2 CC6 / ISO A.10.1) — Implementation: AES-256 envelope encryption; evidence: KMS configuration screenshot, key rotation policy doc, SOC2 auditor note. We'll include that row in the spreadsheet.
[11:55] Jordan: Do you have any timeline or procurement gating we should be aware of?
[11:59] Alexis: We're targeting a pilot in Q1 2026, procurement starts mid-Dec. Main gating items: BAA, controls mapping satisfied, and KMS architecture approved.
[12:12] Jordan: Understood. We'll prioritize the mapping and the BYOK docs.
[12:18] Maya: Quick note — for Dedicated we can also give a staging environment for Elmwood to run a short benchmark and security validation.
[12:27] Tom: That'd be helpful. Any docs on how to run the security validation?
[12:31] Maya: We'll include a playbook with test cases and recommended scripts.
[12:36] Alexis: On the SOC 2 report: will it show vendor-specific exceptions? Any outstanding findings?
[12:44] Maya: The current Type II is clean; we have a few minor control improvements listed but no major exceptions. We'll send the redacted report and a one-page remediation summary.
[12:56] Priya: Regarding data residency again, if we require no US-person access, can you guarantee that?
[13:04] Maya: We can restrict data processing to specific regions and control which SREs have access via RBAC and Just-In-Time access, but guaranteeing no US-person access is tricky for global staff. For strict personnel controls we recommend Private on-prem or using dedicated regional accounts with contractual clauses. We'll document our personnel access processes.
[13:28] Jordan: Anything else from Elmwood side?
[13:31] Alexis: One more: do you have a control for change management / deployment approvals? Our auditors want to see traceable change windows and approvals.
[13:40] Maya: Yes, we have a change management policy, deployment approvals tracked in our CI/CD system with audit trails and release notes. Evidence links will be in the Trust Center.
[13:52] Tom: Ok, let's talk about the follow-up logistics. We need the spreadsheet and the redacted SOC2 by Friday, correct?
[13:59] Jordan: Yes, we'll send those by Friday 2025-11-21.
[14:05] Maya: I'll attach the controls mapping and the BYOK diagram. Also will include the Trust Center request path for the ISO cert and pentest NDA procedure.
[14:17] Alexis: Perfect. We'll review and get back with specific comment rows.

-- Mid call (timestamps continue) --
[20:00] (discussion continued about specific RBAC role names, sample mappings, and evidence types — some slight crosstalk)
[25:40] Priya: For the log format, do you provide JSON logs? We prefer structured logs with ECS-compatible fields.
[25:47] Maya: Yes, we can provide structured JSON logs and we have an ECS-compatible mapping if you want to ingest to Elastic.
[28:10] Tom: About keys, we need to understand whether the envelope encryption adds latency, and what's the impact on throughput.
[28:18] Maya: Envelope encryption adds negligible latency for inference; in Dedicated/Private with local KMS/HSM the RTT is lower. We can provide benchmarks.
[30:05] Alexis: Ok great. Let's recap next steps.
[30:10] Jordan: Recap: Maya will send the redacted SOC2 Type II, ISO cert, controls mapping spreadsheet, BYOK architecture diagram, pentest NDA instructions, and log export playbook by 2025-11-21. Alexis will confirm residency/PHI restrictions by 2025-11-24. Jordan will schedule the follow-up technical deep dive by 2025-11-28.
[30:35] Priya: We'll also want the sample role definitions and a sample audit log export.
[30:41] Maya: Will include those.
[30:44] Alexis: Thanks everyone. If you can include a short one-page summary for procurement (BAA, right-to-audit, SLA bullets), that will help accelerate contracting.
[30:55] Jordan: Absolutely, we'll include procurement bullets.
[31:00] (end of main discussion, casual signoffs)
